item.subject: Advanced Mathematics
item.stem:
Two circles with centres A and B as shown below have radii of 7 cm and 10 cm respectively. If the length of the common chord PQ is 8 cm, what is the length of AB? Show all your work.

[Image: Two intersecting circles with centers A and B]

descriptors: 14.9 or sqrt(84) + sqrt(33) . Method: Pythagorean theorem applied in triangles APS and BPS (S is the midpoint of PQ).

14.9. Method: Trigonometry functions (ratios) used correctly to determine lengths of sides of triangles OR size of angles of triangle that results in determining the length of AB. Note: Most frequently used trigonometric functions are sine and cosine.
Method as in 20 but solution contains a (minor) error in method, or numerical or rounding error.
Method as in 21 but solution contains a (minor) error in method, or numerical or rounding error.
Other partially correct solutions, with minor error.
Method: Pythagorean theorem applied to ΔAPB which is not a right triangle.
Incorrect use of the Pythagorean theorem in a right triangle.
Figure in booklet has been considered accurate and lengths of segments and/or measures of angles have been determined from the diagram.
Crossed-out, illegible, or impossible to interpret

item.scoring_notes:
Note: 1. Since the expected precision is not indicated, every result obtained by a correct method and reasonable and correct rounding should be accepted.
2. If student gives at some stage the correct answer but continues and later makes a numerical (not conceptual) error, ignore this error.
item.figure_description: Two intersecting circles are shown. The smaller circle on the left has its center labeled A, and the larger circle on the right has its center labeled B. A horizontal line segment connects center A and center B. The two circles intersect at two points labeled P (top) and Q (bottom). A vertical line segment connects P and Q, intersecting line segment AB. Line segment AP is drawn and labeled "7 cm", and line segment BP is drawn and labeled "10 cm".

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it.
